forest_08_001.speaker: narrator
forest_08_001.text: Shi Lan put the dawn readings on the table and canceled ignition. The decision took less than a minute after the qualified leaders compared them. Gusts above the patch exceeded the approved range, while the hollow still held smoke under its cold air layer. Either condition was enough. The senior worker closed the ignition kit and returned it to storage. Outside, the assembled crew waited for the sentence that would turn their early breakfast into a day different from the one they expected.

forest_08_002.speaker: shi_lan
forest_08_002.text: No ground burn today. The callout and standby terms cover this assembled shift; nobody loses the agreed pay because the conditions failed. We will do only the safe observation, tool, and level-path tasks assigned by the senior worker. Kiln operations may continue under their own keeper and schedule. This cancellation does not make the approved charcoal billets disappear. It does mean the fireline crew has spent a morning waiting, and I will answer for that cost at the review.

forest_08_003.speaker: narrator
forest_08_003.text: A worker asked whether the hollow might clear by noon. Shi Lan said they would observe it, but no one should wait with an ignition expectation. A new decision would require the full conditions and qualified roster again. The worker kicked at the frost, annoyed by paid disappointment. Wen understood the annoyance so visibly that Lin wanted to look away. She was disappointed too. Her shoulders remembered every shovel length as if labor entitled the weather to cooperate.

forest_08_004.speaker: narrator
forest_08_004.text: Long's manager arrived with two grain-house carriers prepared for a later timber turn. He stopped when he saw the closed kit. He said the town circular had already been corrected, but customers would still ask why nothing happened during the possible week. Shi Lan gave him the actual readings and the decision. He asked whether she could phrase it more optimistically. The senior worker said the optimistic phrase was no houses burned. Shi Lan told him to let the manager finish his tea first.

forest_08_005.speaker: narrator
forest_08_005.text: Long came soon after, wearing the better work gloves he had acquired during preparation. He listened to the readings and did not challenge the cancellation. He challenged the cost of assembling the crew before the conditions were known. Shi Lan explained the dawn decision required rested qualified people ready before the possible window, with accepted callout terms. Long asked whether the next plan could reduce that cost. The operational reviewer would examine the scheduling, she said. Today's terms would still be honored.

forest_08_006.speaker: long_qian
forest_08_006.text: Then pay them. I am not asking you to recover the expense from men who came when called. I am asking whether we have arranged the warning and staffing as well as we can. Perhaps the answer is yes and winter is simply expensive. I would like that answer from the reviewer rather than from our collective irritation. My kitchens cannot cook the distinction, but the next budget can. I will bring the question there instead of shouting it at your closed box.

forest_08_007.speaker: narrator
forest_08_007.text: Rong arrived carrying the town office's latest letter. Its writer had heard the flag rumor before the correction and still suspected interference. Rong read the cancellation facts before opening the accusation aloud. He asked whether someone had changed the wind gauge or concealed a route. The senior worker's face hardened. Shi Lan offered the independent observation records and the runner's account. Rong said he wanted those precisely so he could answer his brother. The room's tension eased by a small, grudging amount.

forest_08_008.speaker: narrator
forest_08_008.text: At the assembly point, a worker called Shi Lan afraid of fire. The word carried across the clearing. Lin turned so quickly that her glove caught on a pin. Before she could answer, the senior worker asked the speaker whether he wanted to compare the current conditions with the approved plan. The man said everyone knew the warden's old accident. Shi Lan stood still. Lin felt fury arrive with the seductive simplicity of a person she could oppose.

forest_08_009.speaker: lin_yue
forest_08_009.text: Her old accident is not today's wind reading. If you want to question the decision, question the reading or the approved limit. I watched the hollow holding smoke this morning. So did people who have never seen her scar. I am angry at what you said, and I may be saying this too sharply. But you do not get to turn her injury into evidence that the weather should be ignored. The crew is being paid. Nobody has bought the right to a reckless fire.

forest_08_010.speaker: narrator
forest_08_010.text: The worker flushed and said Lin spoke like someone whose lodging was always assured. She had no quick reply to that. His household depended on the future operation turn, even if today's callout was paid. Shi Lan intervened before Lin found a crueler sentence. The work and renewal questions could be brought to the office; the current decision stood. The worker left for the assigned tool task. Lin freed her caught glove and discovered she had torn its repaired seam.

forest_08_011.speaker: narrator
forest_08_011.text: Wen walked beside her to the wash station. He said he had wanted to answer the man too. Lin asked whether she had helped. He said she had defended the facts and probably made the man hate hearing them from her. She frowned. He said both could be true. She splashed cold water onto her face and laughed without amusement. The forest had given her another occasion to understand a principle less gracefully than she could explain it.

forest_08_012.speaker: wen_cai
forest_08_012.text: I am glad you spoke. I am also glad Shi Lan stopped you before the next sentence. I have been stopped before my next sentence often enough to recognize the mercy. Come carry the spare handles with me. We can do something useful while you decide whether to rehearse a better argument. If you rehearse aloud, I will charge one bean cake per paragraph. My sister says your paragraphs have become longer since you learned to dig.

forest_08_013.speaker: narrator
forest_08_013.text: They took the handles to the level shed. The ordinary kiln crew was working as planned, converting approved billets under the keeper's separate schedule. Smoke rose in a familiar column from the safe vent and flattened farther away over the cold valley. The ground-burn cancellation had not stopped every fire. Lin watched the distinction embodied by two crews doing different work. She wished it were as easy to carry into a public argument as a replacement handle.

forest_08_014.speaker: narrator
forest_08_014.text: At noon, the hollow remained smoky and the upper wind swung again. The observation report confirmed the canceled window. Long's manager sent the plain update, with no suggested ignition hour. Rong copied it to town beside the independent readings. The worker who had accused Shi Lan continued sharpening tools under the senior worker's inspection. He did not apologize. He did the task well. Lin let the good edge remain a good edge without demanding it settle the insult.

forest_08_015.speaker: narrator
forest_08_015.text: Pei met Shi Lan on the lower path and offered a cup of tea. The warden accepted, then stood holding it until Pei told her drinking was permitted. She took a swallow. Pei said the old keeper's office would record any formal complaint about the cancellation. Shi Lan said she expected one. Pei asked whether she wanted company when it arrived. The warden nodded. Lin, watching from the shelter, saw the answer cost her more than the morning's decision had.

forest_08_016.speaker: shi_lan
forest_08_016.text: I know the conditions failed. I do not know whether I have made every scheduling decision well. That is the part I can review without pretending the first fact changes. When he called me afraid, I wanted to tell him fear had kept him alive today. It would have sounded satisfying and made me unbearable. I am afraid sometimes. I also know the plan. I would like to be allowed both facts without giving either man a victory speech.

forest_08_017.speaker: narrator
forest_08_017.text: Pei said the office specialized in unsatisfying facts and could probably accommodate two more. Shi Lan laughed at last. The tea had gone lukewarm. They walked down together to revise the roster for the safe remaining tasks. Lin stayed at the shelter, helping the basket mender stack his repaired rims. He said fire wardens were like basket handles: everyone noticed them chiefly when they failed. Lin asked whether that made his profession more peaceful. He said his customers could be ferocious about baskets.

forest_08_018.speaker: narrator
forest_08_018.text: Late in the afternoon, a runner reported smoke above the excluded ridge. It was too far from the kiln and too thin to match the shelter stove. Shi Lan sent the qualified watch to observe from safe ground and held the preparation crew at its assembly point. Nobody knew yet whether the source was a cooking fire, a smoldering root, or someone ignoring the cancellation. Lin's anger vanished under a colder attention. The forest had introduced an event that no meeting had scheduled.

forest_08_019.speaker: narrator
forest_08_019.text: The watch found a small unauthorized campfire in a sheltered pocket, with embers spreading into dry needles beneath an overhang. No camper remained. The qualified crew contained the edge using the available water and hand tools, then checked the surrounding litter and roots under the senior worker's direction. The fire had not become a broad blaze. Its location made the discovery lucky rather than trivial. A cooking pot and an empty wire spool lay beside the blackened stones.

forest_08_020.speaker: narrator
forest_08_020.text: Shi Lan kept the pot and spool in place until the immediate safety work was complete and the scene could be recorded. The wire looked finer than the road keeper's repair coil. That resemblance still required comparison with the found snare. A footprint led toward the high path, where snow had been kicked over the heel. Wen stared at the empty camp and said someone had been warm here while everyone below argued about whether the warden was too careful.

forest_08_021.speaker: narrator
forest_08_021.text: By dusk, the camp's heat was safely contained under the qualified recheck plan, with a watch assigned for later inspection. The wildlife investigator received word of the spool, pot, and location. The cancellation complaint would now share the office table with an unauthorized fire inquiry. Lin carried the incident account downhill beside Wen. Her torn glove hung from one finger. She had defended the canceled fire in the morning. In the evening, the canceled crew had helped prevent a different fire from growing.

forest_08_022.speaker: narrator
forest_08_022.text: The campfire inquiry began the next morning with an unwelcome distinction. The crew knew where the unauthorized fire had been and what objects remained. It did not know when it had been lit or who had lit it. The wildlife investigator compared the wire spool with the preserved snare. Their diameter and twist were similar, but such wire was sold widely. Similar material supported further inquiry. It did not turn the first man with a grey cap into a proven trapper.

forest_08_023.speaker: narrator
forest_08_023.text: The pot had a cracked handle repaired with a strip of red leather. The village cook recognized the repair because she had lent that strip to a visiting laborer during the last market. She could identify the laborer's lodging, not swear he still owned the pot. The lodging keeper said he had left before dawn two days earlier. He had paid for his room and left a parcel for collection. The investigator asked the keeper to preserve the ordinary registration page.

forest_08_024.speaker: narrator
forest_08_024.text: A charcoal worker recognized the parcel as spare boot leather he had sold to the visitor. Another remembered the visitor asking about naturally shed Hart antlers. None recalled him setting traps. The dealer said several people had asked about his premium after reading the notice. His list of inquiries was informal and incomplete. Shi Lan requested the actual entries and left the gaps visible. Lin could feel the village wanting a face badly enough to sharpen every vague description.

forest_08_025.speaker: narrator
forest_08_025.text: At the square, the worker who had insulted Shi Lan announced that the unauthorized fire proved somebody was interfering with supply. He did not explain how. Long's manager began agreeing until Lin asked whether he meant the fire had caused the morning's wind gusts. The manager stopped. The camp could have worsened local smoke if lit early enough, but the wind alone exceeded the plan. A careless theory was trying to climb into the decision records through a gap left by embarrassment.

forest_08_026.speaker: lin_yue
forest_08_026.text: We can investigate the camp without pretending it changes the morning readings. I was angry yesterday and spoke too sharply to you. That is mine to answer for. The canceled ignition remains justified by the actual gusts. If someone lit an unauthorized fire, that is another hazard, not proof that Shi Lan should have started a larger one. Bring your complaint about scheduling to the review. I will listen without using your insult to make every question you ask look foolish.

forest_08_027.speaker: narrator
forest_08_027.text: The worker stared at her, then said he would bring it. He did not apologize for the scar remark. Lin had hoped her admission would purchase one in return and felt annoyed when it did not. Wen noticed the annoyance later and called her a poor bargainer. She told him she had not been bargaining. He looked at her until she laughed reluctantly. Sometimes the most irritating witness was the person who knew where her generosity had hidden an expectation.

forest_08_028.speaker: narrator
forest_08_028.text: The unauthorized camp stayed under the qualified heat recheck until the crew cleared it. The pot and spool went into the investigator's sealed evidence pack with their locations and handling recorded. The parcel at the lodging remained under the keeper's ordinary custody unless the district office obtained authority for further inspection. Shi Lan sent warning notices about open fires in the refuge approach. They named the rule and reporting point, not a suspect. Lin helped post them before the market grew busy.

forest_08_029.speaker: narrator
forest_08_029.text: At one notice board, an old woman asked whether warming tea now required a magistrate. Lin showed her the permitted shelter stove and explained the excluded camp area. The woman said the board should show that place too. She was right. Lin carried the suggestion back, and the clerk added a simple route sketch. Later, the woman returned with a cup of tea and said the sketch had made her less cross. Lin accepted the tea without asking whether she approved the rest of the commission.

forest_08_030.speaker: narrator
forest_08_030.text: Rong's brother sent another letter, this one proposing to transfer future hauling to a town contractor who claimed faster winter work. Rong read it beside the actual road closure. The contractor's quoted route used the damaged crossing. The date on the quotation was newer than the closure report. Rong requested the contractor's current route verification before considering the offer. He looked weary as he sealed the request. Fast work from a desk was becoming a recurring species of imaginary animal.

forest_08_031.speaker: rong_sui
forest_08_031.text: I am not rejecting every proposal from town. My brother will say I am. I am asking this contractor to show how he intends to move the wagon over a crossing that our district crew has closed. If he has a valid alternate plan, we should examine it. If he only has confidence, I do not want to buy it by the bag. The paper boat has survived longer than some of these proposals, and its builder made no claim that it could carry charcoal.

forest_08_032.speaker: narrator
forest_08_032.text: The contractor replied that the driver had used an old route name for a newer lower crossing. The error was corrigible, but the revised carriage price was higher and the available wagon capacity smaller. Pei added the offer to proposed alternatives, outside confirmed local output. Rong's brother had hoped it would make the valley office look slow. Instead it gave the commission another possible tool, with limits. Lin liked that an argument could accidentally bring useful information without becoming correct.

forest_08_033.speaker: narrator
forest_08_033.text: Meanwhile, the kiln keeper completed another accepted firing under the ordinary schedule. The dry bags were counted against the remaining seasonal output, with cooling losses and fines kept separate. The first revised delivery income triggered the foreman's four-copper installment. He paid it without asking the voluntary contributors for more. Wen's uncle watched the receipt written and put his own contribution copy away at last. His cap looked relieved to lose one item of responsibility.

forest_08_034.speaker: narrator
forest_08_034.text: The shoulder-injured worker came to the clinic for his follow-up. Pain was easing under rest, but lifting remained restricted. The temporary light task available to him involved sorting tags and mending empty sacks, at the stated agreed rate. He accepted after asking whether the review could lead to his ordinary task later. The answer was yes if medical clearance and work demand allowed. He said he disliked the condition, then signed. Disliking it did not prevent him from needing the job.

forest_08_035.speaker: narrator
forest_08_035.text: Lin joined the sack-mending bench for one shift. Her stitches were slower than the injured worker's and considerably uglier. He told her she pulled the thread as if interrogating it. She loosened her grip. He showed her how the seam would sit flatter. For the first time since she had watched him cry beside the branch stack, he sounded absorbed rather than ashamed. At the end of the shift, he held up her repaired sack and pronounced it survivable.

forest_08_036.speaker: narrator
forest_08_036.text: Wen arrived with lunch and asked whether the sack would be allowed near respectable charcoal. The worker said it was already more respectable than Wen's paper Hart. Lin told Wen he had been outnumbered by craft professionals and should retreat. He retreated as far as the next stool and ate. The old insult in the clearing seemed distant for a while. Outside, the wind pressed the bare branches into one another, still unsuitable for the proposed surface fire.

forest_08_037.speaker: narrator
forest_08_037.text: The district road crew completed its support replacement later that week. The crossing would reopen only after the final load and drainage checks, so the closure stayed posted. The empty-cart driver received instructions for safe recovery of his vehicle without using the deck before clearance. Long's grain suppliers continued on the paid lower route. Nobody treated a visible new timber as permission to hurry a wagon across it. Lin walked past the road report without feeling compelled to understand every joint.

forest_08_038.speaker: narrator
forest_08_038.text: The fire scheduling review convened with the operational reviewer, Shi Lan, crew representatives, and the buyers' offered questions. It found the dawn callout reasonable under the possible window but recommended a cheaper preliminary observation turn on later days when the forecast was marginal. A full ready crew would still be required before a real ignition opportunity. The canceled shift's agreed wages stood. The worker who complained about cost looked pleased that his question had changed something without overturning the safety decision.

forest_08_039.speaker: shi_lan
forest_08_039.text: We will use the preliminary turn where it fits. Thank you for asking the scheduling question plainly today. I did not enjoy yesterday's accusation, and I do not have to enjoy it to accept a better arrangement. The next observation roster will be posted tonight. If you want that smaller paid turn, apply through the ordinary list. It will not require you to agree that I am courageous. I would prefer you notice the wind.

forest_08_040.speaker: narrator
forest_08_040.text: The worker nodded. After the review, he approached Shi Lan by the door and said the scar remark had been unfair. The apology was brief and private. Lin was across the room, stacking cups, and heard only its last word. Shi Lan's shoulders changed. Lin found herself glad without needing the apology repeated for her benefit. Wen took two cups from the stack before she dropped them through inattention. He said good news could apparently make her clumsy too.

forest_08_041.speaker: narrator
forest_08_041.text: That evening Pei's office received a folded copy purporting to confirm the northern boundary. Its sender claimed the land office had settled the disputed segment earlier than expected. The seal resembled the office's usual mark, but the wording contradicted the retained road order and omitted the planned second field check. Pei did not post it as permission. She sent a direct verification request to the land office and put the folded copy in the pending file. The forest had supplied another dangerous convenience.

forest_08_042.speaker: narrator
forest_08_042.text: Lin saw the copy only after Pei invited her to compare its public clauses. Three added words made the old road line sound like a permanent land boundary. The hand was neat, the paper ordinary, the implication profitable. Wen stared at it and said the foreman would love it. Pei said loving a page did not establish who wrote it. She locked the pending file. Outside, the cold hollow still held snow while the sunny paths thawed, indifferent to what a forged-looking sentence hoped to own.

forest_08_043.speaker: narrator
forest_08_043.text: The land office's first acknowledgment arrived two days later: the folded confirmation had not been issued from its current docket. A fuller comparison would follow with the inspector's visit. Pei posted the acknowledgment and kept the northern hold in place. The copy's sender was a forwarding agent in town, not its identified author. Rong recognized the agent as someone his brother had used for supplier introductions. He sent a request for the document's actual source before the brother could defend it as helpful.

forest_08_044.speaker: narrator
forest_08_044.text: The foreman had already heard of the supposed confirmation and came angry about the continued hold. Pei showed him the acknowledgment. He said the office always took longer to deny something than a man could take to cut a tree. Shi Lan answered that this was exactly why the hold remained. He looked toward Wen, hoping for family support through the crew. Wen kept his hands on his own work slip and said he wanted lawful work, not a faster mistake.

forest_08_045.speaker: narrator
forest_08_045.text: Afterward the foreman assigned Wen to the ordinary licensed stock turn and made no direct threat. His manner was cold enough that Wen felt one anyway. Lin accompanied him to the yard because they had the same delivery task, not because she could guarantee how the foreman would behave. The keeper set them to accepted bags under his own schedule. By noon, Wen had stopped anticipating an argument every time a footstep approached. The absence of a threat had become work of its own.

forest_08_046.speaker: wen_cai
forest_08_046.text: I do not want you to walk beside me forever because someone might be unpleasant. I liked having you there today. Those statements are related in a way I cannot explain neatly. My sister says friendship is partly knowing when to stop explaining. She would be delighted if she heard me quote her. Please tell her I thought of it myself. No, do not. She would recognize the theft and charge me for it.

forest_08_047.speaker: narrator
forest_08_047.text: Lin told him she had enough trouble tracking real stolen things without laundering sayings. He laughed and took the next bag. Their route crossed the square where the dealer's revised notice now offered only lawful shed material under verified conditions. The intact-pair premium had been withdrawn during the inquiry. Two men complained that the district office was ruining a chance to earn money. Another asked whether the original premium had ever been real. Nobody had a persuasive answer.

forest_08_048.speaker: narrator
forest_08_048.text: The lodging keeper sent word that the visitor with the repaired pot had returned for his parcel. By the time the investigator arrived, he had left again, paying his remaining charge. The keeper had asked about the camp as instructed; he denied knowing it and said he had sold the pot before moving on. He named a market buyer only by appearance. The account was recorded. It did not establish innocence or guilt. The investigator issued a request to locate the buyer without publishing an accusation.

forest_08_049.speaker: narrator
forest_08_049.text: The parcel contained boot leather, as the seller had said, after the visitor opened it in the keeper's presence to show what he was collecting. No wire or antlers were seen. Lin had hoped the parcel would resolve the inquiry and felt foolish when it proved so ordinary. Pei said most parcels were ordinary, which was fortunate for everyone who carried one. She asked Lin to stop staring at the sealed evidence list and help find the missing lamp-oil invoice.

forest_08_050.speaker: narrator
forest_08_050.text: The invoice was in the basket mender's returned work slip bundle. He had wrapped the repaired handle samples in it to protect them from dirt. Pei retrieved it with a look of despair at the world's inventive use of administrative paper. Lin cleaned the oil mark from the corner carefully. The basket mender promised not to repeat the offense, then asked whether the blank reverse could still be used after payment. Pei said yes. Waste offended her almost as much as disappearance.

forest_08_051.speaker: narrator
forest_08_051.text: Wen's sister set her marriage meal for the tenth commission week, five weeks ahead. The roof was dry, the door shut, and the remaining wall work had a realistic plan. She refused to wait for every winter debt to vanish. Her intended husband agreed, looking relieved enough that the aunt teasing him asked whether he had thought marriage required a fully audited house. He said he had thought it required a house his bride wanted to enter. That silenced the teasing for once.

forest_08_052.speaker: narrator
forest_08_052.text: Wen began saving from his ordinary shifts again. He wanted a good meal without another advance, and his sister told him a smaller feast would not disgrace her. He said he knew. Then he asked the cook about the cost of a larger one. The cook referred him to the sister first. Lin, present with a washing bucket, burst out laughing. Wen looked betrayed. His sister later chose the smaller meal and added one favorite dish, which was more effective than all his private grandeur.

forest_08_053.speaker: narrator
forest_08_053.text: Long offered to sell the feast grain at the posted ordinary rate and hold the accepted quantity until the stated collection date. Wen declined credit and paid a small deposit from his wages. The remaining amount would be due under the usual terms. Long looked pleased to receive a transaction that required no special speech. He asked whether there would be music. Wen said Pei's old song might appear if the family could find its missing second verse before the niece replaced another public official with a vegetable.

forest_08_054.speaker: narrator
forest_08_054.text: Pei said she knew the second verse and had omitted it at the frost meal because it was embarrassingly romantic. The niece demanded it immediately. Pei refused in the office. Shi Lan asked whether romance was now a protected private record. The keeper told her not to be impertinent. That evening she sang the verse in the kitchen, very softly. It concerned a traveler who promised to return before the road iced. Lin listened with more attention than the teasing deserved.

forest_08_055.speaker: narrator
forest_08_055.text: The preliminary weather turn began under the revised cheaper roster. Two qualified observers and a rested messenger checked the needed points before a full operation callout would be considered. The next possible days remained poor: gusting upper air, damp fuel at the edge, and the smoke-holding hollow. The crew did other authorized work instead of assembling for ignition. The scheduling change saved expense without changing the conditions for an actual burn. The complaining worker took one observation turn and returned with useful readings.

forest_08_056.speaker: narrator
forest_08_056.text: The worker gave Shi Lan the report without awkwardness. Lin did not mention his apology. He told Wen that standing on the upper ridge before dawn made every dry timetable feel warmer than it deserved. Wen said the expensive practice floor might offer a similar enlightenment. The worker asked whether it had a stove. Lin said no. He declared the forest superior by one stove and refused to discuss metaphysics further until lunch.

forest_08_057.speaker: narrator
forest_08_057.text: On the sixth week's first morning, a hard frost reached the sunny road as well as the hollow. The temporary migration arrangements had become familiar, perhaps too familiar. At the gathering shelter, the carrier roster's early turn filled quickly. An elderly woman chose to wait for the later turn, but her grandson slipped away to retrieve a small bundle before the watch returned. He knew the path from summer. Winter had changed its length by making every safe step slower.

forest_08_058.speaker: narrator
forest_08_058.text: The watch noticed the missing boy when the grandmother asked where he had put the rope. Shi Lan stopped the next gathering group and sent the qualified search pair along the wider route while another checked the narrow approach from safe ground. Lin joined the village-side messenger task, carrying the description and last known time to the lower shelter. Her stomach tightened before she reached the first bend. The boy was not a rumor about somebody else's careless choice. He was absent from a warm room.

forest_08_059.speaker: narrator
forest_08_059.text: They found his bundle on the path and his cap farther uphill. Beyond it, the snow had collapsed over a shallow drainage ditch. A watchman called and heard a weak answer. The boy had slipped into water hidden beneath the snow and climbed out onto the bank, then become too cold and confused to follow the safe return. The search pair reached him from stable ground with a dry wrap. Lin ran for the clinic assistant by the clear route, keeping the message short enough to arrive intelligible.

forest_08_060.speaker: narrator
forest_08_060.text: The clinic assistant met them at the shelter. The boy was conscious but shivering violently, his wet clothes stiffening at the edges. She directed the team to move him gently into the warmer room, remove the wet layers with privacy, and use the available dry insulation while she assessed him. Nobody asked him to explain himself first. His grandmother sat outside the screen, gripping the spare rope so tightly that Lin had to offer her a cloth before the strands cut her palm.

forest_08_061.speaker: narrator
forest_08_061.text: The grandmother kept saying she had told him to wait. Lin heard herself about to say that was not her fault, then stopped because neither knew enough to make the sentence useful. She offered water and stayed beside her. Behind the screen, the assistant asked the boy simple questions and monitored his condition. Shi Lan arranged the onward clinic transfer under the medical advice. The forest's cold had finally crossed into a room where every minute sounded different.

forest_08_062.speaker: narrator
forest_08_062.text: Wen brought the clinic's transport cart, stocked with warm blankets and wrapped hot-water flasks along the clear lower route with its assigned driver. His knee was cleared for the work now, and he moved carefully rather than quickly for show. The boy traveled wrapped and attended, his grandmother beside him. Lin carried the abandoned bundle to the shelter and left it for the family. It looked absurdly small. No amount of wood in it could explain why a child had tried to carry winter home alone.

forest_08_063.speaker: narrator
forest_08_063.text: At evening, the boy remained under clinic observation, improving enough to answer his grandmother clearly but not cleared for home. The assistant would review him through the night. Shi Lan suspended the early unsupervised gathering approach pending the next morning's access review. The wider route remained available with the funded watch and carrier turns. Lin returned to the lodging with her gloves still damp from the rope. The niece looked up from her paper animals and asked why everyone had stopped singing.

forest_08_064.speaker: narrator
forest_08_064.text: Lin told the niece that a boy had become very cold and was being cared for. The girl asked whether the Hart had done it. Lin said no. The answer mattered immediately; the child moved the paper Hart back beside its dog rather than into the corner where she had put frightening things. Shi Lan watched from the doorway. Later, she thanked Lin for not allowing the day's fear to acquire an animal simply because an animal was already available.

forest_08_065.speaker: narrator
forest_08_065.text: The watch checked the collapsed ditch crossing and closed that local shortcut with a clear board and physical barrier. The boy's summer memory had led him onto snow covering an unsafe hollow. The closure did not block the wider permitted route. Two gatherers helped place the barrier and asked why the ditch had not been marked earlier. Shi Lan said the review would answer that. She did not offer the boy's disobedience as a complete defense of the route.

forest_08_066.speaker: narrator
forest_08_066.text: At the clinic, the grandmother slept for a short while on a bench after the assistant insisted she accept a blanket. Lin stayed until the assigned family support arrived, then left. She had begun to enjoy being the person who remained latest, and the recognition made her uncomfortable. Remaining could help; remaining could also turn someone else's vigil into her proof of devotion. Tonight the grandmother had company she knew better. Lin's own bed was not a betrayal.

forest_08_067.speaker: wen_cai
forest_08_067.text: You look like you are arguing with sleep. I recommend losing. I tried winning after the kiln accident and became useless before breakfast. The boy is at the clinic with the people who know how to watch him. The barrier is up. The watch roster is filled. If you have another actual task, name it. If you only have a feeling that the night would be kinder if you suffered through it awake, come sit down and let me bring you tea.

forest_08_068.speaker: narrator
forest_08_068.text: Lin sat down. He brought tea too weak to deserve its name and apologized. She drank it anyway. Outside, the night was colder than the room's small brazier could imagine, but the lodging roof held and the stove drew cleanly under its ordinary check. Shi Lan put the niece to bed without a story about dangerous forests. She told the story of the flying kettle, whose chief adventure was remembering where it had left its lid.

forest_08_069.speaker: narrator
forest_08_069.text: The council met early the next morning. The access review found the carrier demand exceeded the first turn's capacity on hard-frost days. Families sometimes arrived believing early collection guaranteed early carrying. The roster had not made its limit clear enough. A second bounded early carrier turn could be funded by moving an unstarted sign-painting expense and using the access allowance's remaining margin. Shi Lan proposed it with a clear capacity notice and the ditch closure maintained.

forest_08_070.speaker: narrator
forest_08_070.text: The gathering households accepted the added turn, though one man asked whether all future cold days would require another meeting. Pei said recurring hard-frost arrangements would be posted once reviewed, reducing the need to improvise each morning. The watch would also tell arriving families when a turn was full before they sent someone ahead. The grandmother's account would be heard later when she wished. The child would not be brought to the office to make the improvements seem officially earned.

forest_08_071.speaker: narrator
forest_08_071.text: Long lent the second available handcart during its accepted idle interval, with a paid carrier assigned from the approved roster. The cook asked who would move her grain sacks meanwhile. The ordinary kitchen carrier remained on that job; the borrowed cart was the spare lower-yard one. Long showed her which. She nodded, satisfied by a specific object rather than a promise about generosity. Lin took the cart to the watch and noticed that one handle needed smoothing before it blistered another hand.

forest_08_072.speaker: narrator
forest_08_072.text: The basket mender wrapped the handle with a repaired leather strip. Wen helped him fit it, then took the cart for a level test. The load stayed within the posted rating. In the square, the woman who had objected to the late carrying turn asked to inspect the new timing. She found it usable and said so. Shi Lan looked more relieved by that sentence than by the whole previous meeting. Lin remembered to deliver it plainly, without making the woman sound converted.

forest_08_073.speaker: narrator
forest_08_073.text: At noon, the clinic reported the boy's temperature and alertness had improved under ordinary care, but his cold-injured toes and painful ankle required further observation. Home would wait. The grandmother asked for her abandoned bundle, not because the boy needed it beside the bed but because the family stove still needed wood. The watch delivered it through the revised carrier turn. Lin saw how an emergency could end for a search crew while continuing in a kitchen they had never entered.

forest_08_074.speaker: narrator
forest_08_074.text: Pei received a letter addressed to Lin by the lower-road courier. The handwriting on the outside was her mother's, familiar enough to make the whole office seem suddenly far away. It answered Lin's letter from two weeks earlier, returning along the route address she had paid to use. Lin tucked it inside her coat until her shift ended. She wanted to read it where she could stop being useful for a little while.

forest_08_075.speaker: narrator
forest_08_075.text: She opened it beside the lodging window as snow began again. Her mother had written about a cracked basin, a neighbor's stubborn rooster, and the small space left on the shelf where Lin's cup used to stand. At the end she asked when the next visit might be possible, accepting that the answer depended on work and roads. Lin read that line three times. Beyond the glass, the hollow's winter and the season's winter had become indistinguishable in the falling white.
